title: Flashcard deck
description: The contract between Claude's extraction pass and the renderer. All three card types are fixed here from the start so that implementing a type later is never a breaking schema change.

id.description: Stable, unique name for this deck. Must stay the same across re-renders, because the player uses it to find a learner's earlier progress.

title.description: Human-readable deck title, shown in the player.

source.description: Where the cards were extracted from: a file path, a URL, or a short description.

cards.description: Card ids must be unique within the deck. Uniqueness is enforced by the validator, not expressible here.

nonEmptyString.description: At least one non-whitespace character. A whitespace-only value would render as a blank card face.

slug.description: Lowercase kebab-case, so it is safe to use as a storage key.

hint.description: Optional nudge, hidden until the learner asks for it. Requesting a hint is recorded so the review screen can separate 'knew it' from 'needed a hint'.

explanation.description: Optional reasoning shown after the card is answered.

card.description: Discriminated by the 'type' field. The validator branches on 'type' before checking anything else.

basicCard.description: Prompt on the front, answer on the back. The learner reveals the answer and grades themselves.

mcqCard.description: Multiple choice. The correct answer and the wrong options are separate fields, so a card cannot have zero or two correct answers. The renderer combines and shuffles them, so the position of the answer is never learnable.

distractors.description: Wrong options. One distractor expresses a true/false card; two to four is the usual range.

clozeCard.description: Fill in the blank. Answers are written inline in the prompt as {{answer}}, in the position they belong, so the text and its answers cannot fall out of step. Write {{answer|also accepted|also this}} to accept more than one spelling.

prompt.description: Must contain at least one {{answer}} blank.
